checks.what: UkrSSR gains Western Ukraine (L'viv, Ivano-Frankivsk, Ternopil, Volyn, Rivne; 369 cells, about 93,000 km2, close to the four pre-war voivodeships) from the Union in 1939-11. The page has 'In November 1939 the Soviet government annexed the entire Polish territory under its control' and 'appended the annexed territories to the Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Lithuanian SSRs'. Trial: 347 cells go to the republic on 1 Jan 1940; 342 were Union-direct before. In 1941 the General Government's gain of Eastern Galicia from the UkrSSR (ledger/2) now finds 178 cells, up from 27, and the 171 nobody cells of 1942-43 are gone. 1944: 349 republic cells against 198 before. Nothing breaks.

Kirghiz SSR gains the Union-held cells of Kyrgyzstan in 1937-01. The page has 'On 5 December 1936 ... it became a separate constituent republic of the USSR'. January 1937 bridges the 1936 year-end snap, which the note says, at confidence 2. Trial, 1 Jan 1940: 659 of 660 cells are the republic's (593 before); 66 Union cells moved, none from anyone else. Same through 1959.

MSSR gains Moldova without Transnistria (118 cells, about 29,800 km2, the six Bessarabian counties) from the Union in 1940-08. The page has 'on 2 August 1940, the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic was established on the main part of the annexed territory'. Side effect: Romania's 1941-07 gain from the Union (ledger/12) now finds nothing, so in 1941-43 the land is drawn as the MSSR's under Romanian occupation (118 cells). Before, it was Romania's land 'occupied' by the MSSR, an inverted status. The page itself says 'The Axis forces completed the occupation of these territories by 26 July 1941', so the new drawing matches the page better. In 1944-59 all 130 Moldovan cells are the MSSR's; before, 111 were Union-direct and 32 nobody's at the end of 1944.

UkrSSR gains Chernivtsi oblast and Budjak (31 + 52 = 83 cells, about 21,000 km2) from the Union in 1940-08. The page names 'Northern Bukovina, Hertsa region and larger parts of Hotin ..., Ismail, and Cetatea Alba counties' as allotted to the Ukrainian SSR, in the 2 August 1940 passage; it does not date the allotment separately. The gazetteer's Budjak does not overlap Moldova. Trial: 81 cells move in 1940. In 1941-43 they are drawn as the UkrSSR's under Romanian occupation (UkrSSR ledger/39); in 1944 they are the republic's.

UkrSSR gains the Union-held cells of Ukraine in 1944-01. The page gives 26 August to 23 December 1943 and 'Soviets reclaim left-bank Ukraine, including the city of Kiev and Donets basin'. January 1944 bridges the 1943 year-end snap, and the note says so. Trial: exactly 1,000 Union cells move. Crimea lies outside the gazetteer's Ukraine and stays RSFSR land until 1954, untouched. The handover of the 1922 Union-direct core at this date is a modelling bridge, which the note admits.

BSSR gains the Union-held cells of Belarus in 1944-08. The page has '22 June - 19 August 1944', the infobox 'Red Army retakes all of Byelorussian SSR' and 'Minsk liberated on 4 July'. Trial: Belarus is 925/925 the republic's from the end of 1944 to 1959; before, 753 were Union-direct and 165 nobody's in 1944. The Bialystok side effect (41 cells to Poland at the 1945 snap) moves them toward the post-war border.

MSSR gains Moldova from the Union in 1944-09. The page has '20-29 August 1944' and 'Soviet control over Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, which had been occupied by the USSR in 1940, was re-established'. With events/13 in force, the MSSR keeps Bessarabia through 1941-44, so in the trial this entry moves no cells. It is harmless insurance, but its note's figures (111 Union-direct cells) describe the published state, not the patched one.

LSSR gains Ostland's remaining Lithuanian cells (115: Alytus/Marijampole in the south, Panevezys/Utena in the north-east) in 1944-11. The page has '14 September - 24 November 1944' and 'resulted in the expulsion of German forces from Estonia and Lithuania', so November is the latest possible date. The Bagration infobox ('most of Lithuania' retaken by 19 August) suggests much of this land was regained earlier; the note flags this at confidence 2. Year-end drawing is the same either way. Trial: Lithuania is 296/296 the LSSR's from 1944 to 1959; before, 115 cells were Ostland's in 1944 and Union-direct from 1945.

UkrSSR gains the Union-held cells of Ukraine in 1945-01, bridging the 1944 year-end snap. Trial: 80 cells, mostly on the Dniester left bank in Odessa oblast, plus about 20 near 48-49N 25-26E; Crimea and Transcarpathia are untouched. The note quotes the Jassy-Kishinev page ('Soviet control ... re-established'), and that sentence is there, but the source field named the Bessarabia occupation page, which does not contain it.
checks.fix: source changed to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Jassy%E2%80%93Kishinev_offensive and a review line added to the note; --check-patch p1940-p1949: 29 ok

checks.what: Kazakh SSR gains 25 Union-held cells of Kazakhstan on the Chinese border in 1945-01, bridging the 1944 year-end snap that took them from the republic. The page has 'on 5 December 1936 it was elevated to the status of a Union-level republic' and an area of '2,717,300 square kilometres'. Trial: 25 Union cells move; the 5 East Turkestan/PRC cells are untouched. The note is honest about confidence 2.

kingdom-of-greece_1949 (1949-1962) becomes adjust: Cliopatria 1949 plus country Greece. That adds 64 cells to the shape's 390 and keeps 10 shape cells outside the polygon, which were already the kingdom's. No other window overrides this shape (patch-overrides.csv lists only kingdom-of-greece_1963 for p1960-p1969). The Dodecanese page has 'formally united with Greece by the 1947 Peace Treaty with Italy'. The Greek Civil War page has the 16 October ceasefire. The Greek junta page has 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels' in 1967; that support is thin, but the claim (the kingdom held its whole country 1949-62) is not in doubt. Trial: 57 nobody cells plus 1 Turkish and 1 Yugoslav border cell inside the Greek polygon go to Greece in 1949. Greece is 442/444 from 1950 to 1959; the 2 Bulgarian-held cells are kept by others.

patch_check: p1930-p1939: 8 entries, 8 ok; p1940-p1949: 29 entries, 29 ok (after the events/19 source fix). Trials --trial p1940-p1949 and --trial p1950-p1959: every entry applied. Ukraine 2354-2355/2360, Belarus 925/925, Moldova 130/130, Lithuania 296/296, Kyrgyzstan 659/660, Greece 442/444 the right owner from 1950 to 1959. Stage deleted.
problems: events/13 and /14 make Romania's 1941-07 gain from the Union (kingdom-of-romania ledger/12, and union ledger/23) move nothing: Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina are now drawn 1941-43 as the MSSR's and UkrSSR's under Romanian occupation, not as Romanian land. This agrees with the page ('completed the occupation of these territories by 26 July 1941') and replaces a published drawing with the status inverted (Romania's land occupied by the MSSR). The orchestrator may still want one convention for Romanian-held Bessarabia 1941-44.
p1940-p1949 events/17 settles nothing in the trial (made redundant by events/13); its note's cell counts describe the published state.
p1960-p1969 events/2-8 and p1950-p1959 events/5-7 (written around earlier gaps) now settle nothing or almost nothing. The seam agent reported this too; withdrawing them is the orchestrator's call.
The 1922 Union-direct cores of the Ukrainian and Byelorussian SSRs (1922-1939/44) remain; they belong to the p1920-p1929 patch file, as the seam agent says.
